staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash against this staged vulnerable checkout. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `310c81aaa20b7328ce7a354897db817f8becac3a`, but the prepared workspace source used for the crash is the staged commit above, which still contains the unfixed `++it` / `(*it).tokens[0]` version-parse path shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502140 (assimp): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502140
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 4123-byte witness (sha256 `e1eabbe1f403197b646166c3aede29445321c2a07b2d47b47cabba8a1b78ed63`) first enters project code when `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory()` wraps the attacker buffer in `MemoryIOSystem`. Because the fuzz harness passes a null hint, Assimp synthesizes the memory filename `$$$___magic___$$$.`, so `LWSImporter::CanRead()` falls back to magic-token detection and reads the first four bytes `LWMO` from that in-memory stream to admit the input to the LightWave Scene Importer. `InternReadFile()` then copies the same bytes into `mBuffer`, preserving the prefix `LWMO\n\0`, and `root.Parse()` stops at the embedded NUL after materializing only one top-level child whose `tokens[0]` is `LWMO`. `InternReadFile()` initializes `it` to that only child, sets `motion_file = true`, bypasses the `LWSC` rejection guard, increments `it` once to `root.children.end()`, and immediately executes `strtoul10((*it).tokens[0].c_str())` without checking `it == root.children.end()`. The saved AddressSanitizer report records a stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at `code/AssetLib/LWS/LWSLoader.cpp:540`, 8 bytes past stack object `root` in the same frame, and the staged patch fixes this path by inserting `if (it == root.children.end() || (*it).tokens[0].empty()) { ... return; }` before the version parse.

source.description: First on-path project consumption of the fuzzer buffer. `ReadFileFromMemory()` converts the attacker bytes and length into the active in-memory IO handler later reused for signature matching and importer reads.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 4123-byte witness at `gt_results/arvo_42502140/poc` (sha256 `e1eabbe1f403197b646166c3aede29445321c2a07b2d47b47cabba8a1b78ed63`). Its first six bytes are `4c 57 4d 4f 0a 00` (`LWMO\n\0`). At line 495 Assimp consumes that buffer and length by wrapping them in `MemoryIOSystem`, so later `CanRead()` and `TextFileToBuffer()` reopen the same attacker-controlled bytes from memory.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After `++it` has already advanced past the only parsed child, this same-line member access dereferences the past-the-end iterator while fetching the version token string.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at this exact line, and the frame report identifies stack object `root` in `Assimp::LWSImporter::InternReadFile` as the overflowed object.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The version parse uses `it` immediately after `++it` without first checking whether the increment exhausted `root.children`. The staged patch adds `if (it == root.children.end() || (*it).tokens[0].empty()) { ... return; }` before this dereference.
root_cause.note: On the saved witness, step 6 initializes `it` to the only parsed `LWMO` child and step 9 advances it to `root.children.end()` before this line runs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The in-memory IO wrapper that retains the exact attacker buffer and length for later header inspection and for the LWS importer's full-file read.
tainted_value_origin.note: The same memory-backed stream is reopened first by `LWSImporter::CanRead()` to observe the leading `LWMO` bytes and later by `TextFileToBuffer()` to copy `LWMO\n\0...` into `mBuffer`.

parser_admitted.description: By this dispatch call the memory-backed witness has already passed Assimp's format matching and entered the LightWave Scene Importer. Stage 01's saved log says `Found a matching importer for this file format: LightWave Scene Importer.`, which grounds that the witness reached the LWS importer path before the crash.

fine_trace.note: Source. `ReadFileFromMemory()` consumes the attacker-controlled `pBuffer` and `pLength` by creating a `MemoryIOSystem` and installing it as the active IO handler. Every later open of the synthesized memory file aliases this same witness.

The caller asks importers to classify `$$$___magic___$$$.`; because `ReadFileFromMemory()` normalized the null hint to an empty suffix, `GetExtension(pFile)` is empty and `CanRead()` falls through to `CheckMagicToken()`. The memory-backed stream from step 1 yields the first four bytes `LWMO`, so the LWS importer accepts this input and control later reaches `InternReadFile()`.
`InternReadFile()` reopens the same memory-backed file and copies all 4123 bytes into `mBuffer`, preserving the prefix `LWMO\n\0` and appending a trailing binary zero for later text parsing.

The first top-level parse iteration materializes the witness prefix `LWMO` as the first child's name token. That token later drives both the `LWMO` motion-file branch and the `LWSC` rejection guard in `InternReadFile()`.

After the first `LWMO` line, `SkipLine()` advances `dummy` to the witness's embedded `\0`, and `SkipSpacesAndLineEnd()` then returns false at that NUL. `root.Parse()` therefore stops with exactly one top-level child in `root.children`; no second child is created for the file-format version line.

With `root.children` holding only the singleton parse result from step 5, the iterator initialization makes `it` point to that lone `LWMO` element. The next predicates and the later increment all operate on this iterator state.
Because `it` still references the only parsed child and that child's token is `LWMO`, the importer sets `motion_file = true`. This state is what later suppresses the `LWSC` rejection path.

The malformed file would ordinarily be rejected here because its first token is not `LWSC`, but the earlier `motion_file = true` makes this guard false on the saved witness. Control therefore continues into the version-reading code even though the parse tree still has only the single `LWMO` child.

Step 6 started `it` at the only child proven by step 5. Incrementing once therefore advances `it` from `root.children.begin()` to `root.children.end()`. After this statement, `it == root.children.end()` on the saved witness.

Root cause. The very next statement reuses `it` as if it still referenced a valid child, even though step 9 already made `it == root.children.end()`. The vulnerable source performs no `it == root.children.end()` check before dereferencing here; the staged fix inserts that guard before this line.

Sink. To evaluate the argument to `strtoul10`, C++ first forms `(*it).tokens[0].c_str()`. Because step 9 already left `it == root.children.end()`, this same-line member access dereferences the past-the-end iterator. AddressSanitizer records this as a `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at line 540 and reports the read landing 8 bytes past stack object `root` in the same frame.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch inserts `if (it == root.children.end() || (*it).tokens[0].empty()) { ASSIMP_LOG_ERROR(...); return; }` between `++it;` and the version parse, so the singleton-parse-tree case no longer dereferences `root.children.end()`. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The first project frame in the saved AddressSanitizer stack is `Assimp::LWSImporter::InternReadFile` at `code/AssetLib/LWS/LWSLoader.cpp:540`, which is the sink step anchored above.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The ASan frame report identifies stack object `root` in `InternReadFile` as the overrun object, and the fix hunk adds the missing `it == root.children.end()` guard immediately before the same line. That matches the traced end-iterator dereference on the parsed `root.children` list.

format.name: LightWave Scene motion-file text input
format.contract: The exact staged 4123-byte witness (sha256 `e1eabbe1f403197b646166c3aede29445321c2a07b2d47b47cabba8a1b78ed63`) beginning `4c 57 4d 4f 0a 00` (`LWMO\n\0`). Within this saved witness, the first four bytes `LWMO` are the observed signature that makes `LWSImporter::CanRead()` accept the synthesized `$$$___magic___$$$.` memory file, and the embedded NUL immediately after the newline is the observed edge that makes `LWS::Element::Parse()` materialize exactly one top-level child with `tokens[0] == "LWMO"` and no second version element before `InternReadFile()` increments the iterator. The staged artifacts ground this exact witness and its observed singleton-parse behavior only; they do not establish a broader malformed-LWS trigger contract.
